title: NFTMinterV2 lacks a contract-level reentrancy guard; hooks and ERC1155 receiver callbacks enable cross-dispatcher re-entry
description:
_executeMint performs transferFrom -> price ratchet -> dispatcher.dispatch -> _mint. Two untrusted callbacks fire inside this sequence: (1) dispatcher.dispatch runs hook.onDispatch under the dispatcher's nonReentrant lock, but that lock is per-dispatcher, so the hook is free to call back into NFTMinterV2.mint(differentIndex, ...) or NFTMinterV2.mintFor(...). (2) _mint(recipient, ...) invokes ERC1155Utils.onERC1155Received on contract recipients, which can re-enter NFTMinterV2.mint(...) at the point where config.price has already been ratcheted but the initiating mint has only just completed. NFTMinterV2 itself has no ReentrancyGuard. 

What IS protected: the caller must fund each nested mint (transferFrom pulls from the nested msg.sender), so there is no free-mint path. The same dispatcher cannot re-enter because its own nonReentrant is held while its hook runs. config.price is updated before the external calls, so the CEI ordering prevents double-ratchet abuse on the outer call. 

What is NOT protected: invariants that span multiple dispatchers during a single user call. Future hooks or auth-minter extensions that assume 'one mint per tx per NFTMinterV2' (rate limiting, cumulative accounting, one-entry-per-block style checks) break silently. mintFor (M-01 / M-02 from prior audits) is also re-entrant from ERC1155 receiver callbacks via authorized minters like NFTMigrator.
impact: Defense-in-depth gap. Not currently exploitable for theft or ratchet manipulation in isolation, but stacks dangerously with (a) future non-trivial hooks (the entire point of the V2 hook surface is that owner will add real hooks later), (b) future authorized-minter integrations, and (c) the already-filed mintFor-related medium findings. The nonReentrant lock on the abstract dispatcher is insufficient as a system-wide guard because it only covers the same dispatcher; the NFTMinterV2 contract itself is the natural boundary where a single guard would catch cross-dispatcher paths.
recommendation: Inherit OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard on NFTMinterV2 and apply nonReentrant to the two mint() overloads, mintFor(), and burn(). This is cheap (single SSTORE per call) and future-proofs the contract against any hook or auth-minter surface added later. It does NOT break the per-dispatcher guard; the two layers are complementary.
dedupNote: Unique. Round-02 L-01 and round-03 L-01 flag missing reentrancy guard on NFTMigrator (different contract, different attack surface). This finding targets NFTMinterV2's _executeMint/mint/mintFor with hook + ERC1155-receiver cross-dispatcher reentry — a new surface created by V2 hooks (story-026). Not covered by knownIssues.
sanitizeNote: In V2 focus area (NFTMinterV2 + story-026 hook surface). Re-entry path is permissionless via ERC1155 receiver and hook callbacks — NOT owner-driven. No match against project knownIssues.
classifyNote: C4 regular-audit Low/QA. Finding self-attests 'not currently exploitable for theft or ratchet manipulation in isolation' — caller must self-fund each nested mint (transferFrom from nested msg.sender, no free-mint path), per-dispatcher nonReentrant covers same-dispatcher re-entry, and CEI ordering on config.price prevents double-ratchet. The harm scenarios (cross-dispatcher invariants for rate-limiting / cumulative accounting) require future hooks or future authorized-minter integrations that don't exist in current code. Pure defense-in-depth + future-code speculation. No present-day asset risk or protocol availability impact. Confirm Low.
validityNote: Borderline defense-in-depth + future-code speculation, but composes with present-day filed Medium findings on mintFor reentrancy via authorized-minter ERC1155-receiver callbacks (NFTMigrator). The cross-dispatcher reentry path through ERC1155 onERC1155Received is a real, present-day reachable path — only the impact requires composition. Keep as QA hardening recommendation; appropriate for Low tier.
